title: Professor Harry Messel International Science School (ISS)
description: A fully-funded, two-week residential science program held at the University of Sydney every two years for high-achieving Year 11/12 science students. Around 110 scholars attend each edition -- roughly two-thirds from Australia and one-third nominated from eight partner countries. Students attend lectures by leading scientists, tour research laboratories, and take part in interactive demonstrations. All costs (travel, accommodation, meals, activities) are covered by ISS scholarships funded by the Physics Foundation at the University of Sydney.
cost: Free - fully funded by ISS scholarships (travel, accommodation, meals, and activities covered)
citizenship_restrictions: Australian applicants must be citizens or permanent residents attending school in Australia. International places are by nomination from eight named partner countries only (China, India, Japan, New Zealand, Thailand, Singapore, UK, USA) -- not a general open-international application.
selectivity_evidence: Merit-based selection from a national/partner-country applicant pool down to roughly 110 total scholars (about 70 Australian plus international); requires top STEM/English grades, a school recommendation letter, and a 500-word personal statement; selection panel balances gender, location, school system, and relative opportunity.
current_cycle_label: Biennial -- most recently held 6-19 July 2025; next edition expected mid-2027 with applications opening early 2027 (exact dates not yet published as of 2026-08-21)
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Runs every two years (biennial), not annually -- important for ORYN's deadline engine not to expect a 2026 cycle. Minimum requirement: at least 50% STEM subject load. A detailed official application-criteria PDF exists on the sydney.edu.au domain for deeper detail once the next cycle opens.

title: National Youth Science Forum (NYSF) - Year 12 Program
description: A residential STEM enrichment program for students about to enter Year 12, held every January in Canberra and Brisbane. Participants attend lectures, labs, and site visits with STEM professionals and researchers, and explore university/career pathways in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Formerly known as the National Science Summer School (until 1995).
cost: AUD 3,180 program fee (due October 2026) plus a AUD 70 non-refundable application fee; Access and Equity Scholarships available for students facing financial hardship
citizenship_restrictions: Must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident, and/or studying full-time at an Australian high school. International students are not eligible for the standard application pathway but are invited to email nysf@nysf.edu.au to express interest in alternative participation.
application_requirements: statement of STEM areas of interest
selectivity_evidence: Applications are reviewed by the NYSF Selection Panel; selection is explicitly 'not based solely on academic results' but is a real competitive review, not an automatic or pay-to-attend enrollment.
current_cycle_label: 2027 program: applications closed 23 July 2026, with outcomes advised mid-August 2026; two 2027 sessions run in Canberra (6-14 Jan) and Brisbane (13-21 Jan)
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Two parallel sessions each January (Canberra and Brisbane) -- this record uses the Canberra session dates; Brisbane runs 13-21 Jan 2027. Next cycle (feeding the 2028 program) would be expected to open around mid-2027. The international-student pathway is a direct email inquiry only, not the standard application form -- flag this clearly before recommending to a non-Australian ORYN user.

title: The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award - Australia
organization: The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award - Australia
description: The Australian operating arm of the global Duke of Edinburgh's International Award, a non-formal education framework built around Voluntary Service, Physical Recreation, Skills, and an Adventurous Journey, culminating in Bronze, Silver, and Gold Award levels. Delivered through schools, community organisations, and accredited Duke of Ed Centres rather than a single central application.
cost: Varies by school/operating Centre; not centrally published on the national site
application_requirements: enrollment through a school or accredited Duke of Ed Centre
current_cycle_label: Rolling / continuous enrollment via schools and Duke of Ed Centres -- no fixed annual application deadline
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Age range (14-24) reflects the globally standard Duke of Edinburgh's International Award framework used across all operating countries/territories; the Australia page fetched did not itself restate this figure, so treat it as a well-established structural fact rather than an Australia-specific quote. The fetched page did not confirm whether international students studying in Australia can enrol -- in practice this depends on whether the student's own school runs the Award. No centralized cost was disclosed; fees are set per operating Centre.

title: Insight Creative Writing Competition
description: A free, national creative-writing competition for Australian high school students (Years 7-12), run by independent educational publisher Insight Publications. Entrants submit an original piece of creative writing (optional 2026 theme: 'IGNITE'); each year-level category is judged separately by an acclaimed Australian author. Prize pool exceeds AUD 3,000 across categories.
residency_restrictions: Open to high school students around Australia
application_requirements: original creative writing piece per entry-form guidelines
selectivity_evidence: Entry is free and open to all eligible students; a limited cash prize pool is awarded per year-level category following judging by a panel of published Australian authors (2026 judges include Amelia Mellor, Andre Dao, Romy Ash, Olivia Muscat, Michael Pryor, and Maxine Beneba Clarke) -- a judged award competition rather than a capacity-limited admission.
current_cycle_label: 2026 competition currently open: entries opened 20 March 2026 and close 1 September 2026
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Currently open with roughly 10 days left until the 1 September 2026 deadline as of this research date (2026-08-21) -- a good near-term, low-effort/high-accessibility recommendation for ORYN's Australian users right now.

title: SAKURA Science High School Program
description: A flagship Japanese-government exchange initiative that invites high-achieving high school students (and an accompanying supervisor/teacher) from foreign countries, mainly across Asia, to Japan for a one-week program of lectures with leading scientists (including Nobel laureates), visits to top universities and research institutes such as JAXA and Hokkaido University, and collaborative activities with Japanese peers. Between 2014 and 2024, 67 courses were run for a total of 6,841 participating high school students.
application_requirements: nomination/submission via each country's designated Sakura Science National Contact -- not a direct individual online application
current_cycle_label: Ongoing annual JST invitation program with multiple weeklong course offerings per fiscal year; specific FY2026/FY2027 High School Program deadlines were not confirmed on the official pages fetched during this research pass
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Applications are not submitted directly by individual students -- each participating country has a designated 'National Contact' (coordinating institution) through which students/schools must apply. Widely reported in secondary sources as fully funded by the Japanese government (flights, meals, accommodation), but that specific cost detail was not confirmed via direct fetch of an official page during this pass -- confirm before displaying a cost claim to students. A separate, distinct 'Open Application Program' (Courses A/B/C/D) also exists under the same Sakura Science umbrella with its own multi-round deadlines, but that track explicitly states individual student-level applications are not accepted there either -- institution-to-institution only. Do not conflate the two sub-programs.

title: Taiwan International Science Fair (TISF)
description: An annual (typically January) international pre-college science research fair held in Taipei, organized by the National Taiwan Science Education Center. Domestic and international students in grades 9-12 present original STEM research projects and compete for Young Scientist, First-to-Fourth, and Special Awards, in a format modeled on the Regeneron ISEF structure. The most recently fully-documented edition, TISF 2025 (20-25 January 2025), drew 629 domestic and overseas participants and 234 projects from 29 nations/regions.
application_requirements: selection/award at a qualifying national or regional-affiliate science fair in the student's home country/region (e.g. an ISEF-affiliated fair) -- TISF is not normally directly self-applicable by an individual student without this qualifying step
selectivity_evidence: International participation is by invitation as part of a national delegation, normally earned by winning/placing at a qualifying national-affiliate science fair (analogous to Regeneron ISEF's international-fair pathway); domestically, the 2025 edition narrowed 512 preliminary-round students / 294 projects down to 174 projects advancing to the finals.
current_cycle_label: Held annually each January; most recently confirmed edition TISF 2025 (20-25 Jan 2025); a TISF 2026 edition page exists on the official site but its specific dates were not independently confirmed, and TISF 2027 dates were not found as of 2026-08-21
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: A student cannot simply sign up for TISF individually -- eligibility runs through their home country's affiliated national science fair/organization (e.g. in the US this is the Regeneron ISEF pathway; other countries have their own science-fair bodies). ORYN should present this as the pinnacle event to aim for after winning a national/regional science fair, not a directly-appliable program. Official contact for international teams: Stephanie Wu, tisf@mail.ntsec.gov.tw.

title: NYU Shanghai AI Pre-College Summer Program
description: A two-week, in-person, English-language pre-college summer program at NYU Shanghai's campus for high school students aged 15-18 interested in artificial intelligence. Taught by NYU Shanghai faculty from the Computer Science, Data Science, and Engineering Division alongside the NYU Shanghai Center for Data Science, students build mathematical foundations for AI, gain hands-on experience with Python/NumPy/PyTorch, and study machine learning from linear regression through neural networks and AI agents.
cost: CNY 26,800 per person (covers instruction, meals, and materials; housing and transportation are the participant's own responsibility)
application_requirements: interview as part of admissions review
selectivity_evidence: Official page describes a competitive admissions process including an interview; outstanding students are recognized with awards at final presentations. No numeric acceptance rate was published.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle fully concluded -- program ran 13-24 July 2026 with application rounds that closed 15 March and 30 April 2026; 2027 dates not yet published
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Visa/access caveat: this program is in person on NYU Shanghai's mainland China campus, so non-Chinese participants will need to independently arrange an appropriate visa to enter mainland China for the program dates -- a materially different access requirement than Hong Kong-based programs (many nationalities get visa-free or on-arrival entry to Hong Kong) and should be flagged distinctly in ORYN's matching logic. The official page stated no nationality restriction, so it appears open to international applicants generally, but this should be reconfirmed directly given the visa complexity. This track sits inside NYU Shanghai's broader 'Summer Academy' umbrella -- other pre-college subject tracks may exist there and are worth a follow-up research pass.

title: HKU Summer Institute - Secondary School Programmes
description: The University of Hong Kong's summer offering for secondary school students, spanning Research, Internship, Immersive, and Multi-location programme tracks across multiple grade bands (roughly S1-S6 / Year 8-13). Explicitly open to both local and non-local (international) students, with several multi-week sessions running through the northern-hemisphere summer.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle fully concluded -- the latest 2026 session ran through 3-7 August 2026; 2026 deadlines ranged from an early-bird 7 February 2026 discount through separate non-local/local deadlines in spring 2026; 2027 dates not yet posted
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: HKUSI explicitly markets to both 'Local' and 'Non-local' students, unlike HKUST's flagship iElite track (nomination-only, already in ORYN's database) -- a genuinely more directly-accessible Hong Kong option. Multiple concurrent sessions/tracks exist under this one umbrella (a Residential Hall option requires age 15+); many showed 'Full' status by this research date (2026-08-21), suggesting popular tracks fill well before their stated deadlines -- ORYN should encourage early application once 2027 dates post. Fee/cost information was not disclosed on the pages fetched; check the HKUSI application system directly.

title: HKUST Pre-University Programs
organization: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST)
description: A set of HKUST pre-university tracks for students in Year 11/Grade 10/Form 4 or above, distinct from HKUST's separate nomination-only iElite Scholars Program. Tracks include the Summer Bootcamp for Polymath, credit-bearing Summer Institute courses (e.g. decision-making, chemistry, business risk, microbiology, Android development, human biology, sociology), Thematic-based Programs (entrepreneurship & innovation, discrete mathematics, STEM sensing, AI, smart learning design), a Collaborative Corporate Program with Tencent, and a Regional Program in Shanghai.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle fully concluded and closed to new registrants -- every listed 2026 track (running in the 19-31 July 2026 window) showed 'Full' status by 2026-08-21; applications generally open Oct-Dec for a 31 May deadline the following year; 2027 cycle not yet open
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Distinct from the HKUST iElite Scholars Program already in ORYN's database (join.hkust.edu.hk/ielite), which is nomination-only from invited partner schools. This Pre-University hub is processed first-come-first-served rather than by competitive nomination, making it a more directly-actionable option for a typical ORYN user, though by this research date all 2026 tracks had already filled. Fee/tuition information was not published on the pages fetched -- confirm directly with HKUST before displaying a cost to students.

title: The Hong Kong Award for Young People (AYP)
organization: The Hong Kong Award for Young People
description: The Hong Kong operating authority for the global Duke of Edinburgh's International Award, running non-formal education activities for young people across five sections (including an Adventurous Journey/expedition section), culminating in Bronze, Silver, and Gold awards. Delivered through schools, uniformed youth organisations, and community centres (over 600 'operating units' as of 2026) rather than a single central application. As of 2026, AYP reports 56,445 Bronze, 25,280 Silver, and 3,714 Gold award holders.
application_requirements: enrollment through a school, uniformed group, or community-centre Operating Unit
current_cycle_label: Rolling / continuous enrollment through Operating Units -- no fixed annual application deadline
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Age range (14-24) reflects the globally standard Duke of Edinburgh's International Award framework; not explicitly restated on the specific AYP page fetched, so treat it as a well-established structural fact rather than an AYP-specific quote (same caveat as the Australia Duke of Ed record in this batch). Whether international/expat students studying in Hong Kong can enrol was not addressed on the fetched page -- in practice this depends on whether the student's own school runs the Award as an Operating Unit, which is common at Hong Kong international schools. Cost not disclosed centrally; likely varies by Operating Unit.

title: National Olympiad in AI (NOAI)
description: Singapore's national artificial-intelligence olympiad and official selection pathway to the International Olympiad in AI (IOAI). Run by AI Singapore (a national AI programme supported by Singapore's National Research Foundation and hosted at the National University of Singapore), NOAI covers Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, and programming. A 300-question preliminary MCQ round narrows the field to the top 150 finalists, who sit a Final Assessment at Nanyang Technological University; a further ~50-60 of the strongest performers are selected for NTU-based training toward possible IOAI team representation.
citizenship_restrictions: Open to full-time students under age 20 currently enrolled at a Singapore MOE school (Secondary, Integrated Programme, Junior College, ITE, or Polytechnic) regardless of nationality; home-schooled Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents are also eligible. A foreign national not enrolled at a Singapore school -- and conversely a Singapore citizen studying abroad -- would not qualify.
residency_restrictions: Must be enrolled at a Singapore MOE school (or home-schooled SC/PR)
selectivity_evidence: 300-question preliminary MCQ assessment; only the top 150 performers nationally advance to the NOAI Final Assessment (held at NTU); a further ~50-60 are selected for NTU international-team training toward possible IOAI representation.
current_cycle_label: NOAI 2026 cycle fully concluded -- school interest window ran 15 Sept-28 Nov 2025 and the Final Assessment was held 6 March 2026 at NTU; NOAI 2027 registration not yet announced as of 2026-08-21
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Critical matching-logic nuance: eligibility is based on current enrollment at a Singapore MOE-linked school (Secondary, IP, JC, ITE, or Polytechnic), NOT nationality or citizenship -- surface this to any ORYN user enrolled at a Singapore school regardless of passport, but not to a Singaporean citizen attending school outside Singapore. The IOAI international final that NOAI feeds into was held 2-8 August 2026 in Astana, Kazakhstan, per the official NOAI/IOAI relationship page.
